surveyDefinition.title: Organic Milk — consumer survey (Asia Pacific)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Organic Milk. Every question asks about Organic Milk specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Asia Pacific actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Asia Pacific who buy or use Organic Milk for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. Excluded: Institutional buyers (restaurants, cafeterias, schools); Dairy farmers or processors; People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
respondentBehaviours: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's overall relationship with milk, then narrows to specific usage occasions, frequency, household roles, and the health and lifestyle needs that drive consumption. It then moves through the purchase journey: what triggers a buy, how they learn about options, where they shop, how often they restock, what decides the choice, how much they spend, and whether buying is routine. Next, it explores product expectations: must-have attributes, quality cues, certifications, packaging preferences, trade-offs, and finally value expectations. It closes with sa

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Organic Milk in Asia Pacific — who Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. The consumer audience for organic milk is defined by household grocery shoppers who prioritize health, sustainability, and product quality, and who actively choose organic over conventional milk.
inclusionCriteria: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household
Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months
Consumes milk or serves it to household members
behaviors: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
exclusions: People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives

contextDemographics.geography: Urban and suburban areas with access to specialty grocery stores

assumptions: Organic milk is assumed to be a retail product, not a bulk ingredient
Consumers are assumed to be in regions where organic milk is widely available
The survey targets the end consumer, not retailers or distributors
targetCustomer.note: Respondents match this target customer. Age, income, and brand/company-name items are NOT asked in the questionnaire; they may appear here only as research context.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how often have you or anyone in your household consumed organic dairy milk?
options: Every day or almost every day
A few times in the month

data.label: Every day or almost every day
A few times in the month

questions.insight: Top response: Several times a week (27.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused, eco-conscious, and young professionals drive frequent consumption; budget and rural segments skew to occasional/non-use.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, in which of the following situations was organic dairy milk consumed or served in your household? Select all that apply.
options: In coffee, tea, or other hot beverages
As a standalone drink for children
As a standalone drink for adults
In cooking or baking (e.g., sauces, pancakes)

data.label: In coffee, tea, or other hot beverages
As a standalone drink for children
As a standalone drink for adults
In cooking or baking (e.g., sauces, pancakes)

questions.insight: Top response: With breakfast cereal or oatmeal (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Breakfast and coffee uses are common across most personas; family-oriented personas lift children's standalone drinking; health-focused boost smoothies.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, about how many half-gallon (or 2-liter) containers of organic dairy milk did your household use?
questions.insight: Top response: 2–3 containers (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget families and value seekers cluster in 2-3 containers; heavy users are health-focused and larger families; non-users mirror cp1 non-consumption.

questions.question: Who in your household typically drinks organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: No one in the household drinks it regularly

data.label: No one in the household drinks it regularly

questions.insight: Top response: Adults 18–64 (72.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Adults dominate as primary consumers; budget families and health-focused boost children's share; retired persona adds older adults.

questions.question: Who in your household is primarily responsible for deciding which organic dairy milk to buy?
options: I decide together with my spouse or partner
It varies from week to week

data.label: I decide together with my spouse or partner
It varies from week to week

questions.insight: Top response: I am (45.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Individual decision-making is strong across personas; joint decisions are common in family-oriented segments; children rarely decide.

questions.question: How important is each of the following to your household's decision to drink organic dairy milk rather than conventional dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused, eco-conscious, and luxury buyers weight 'very/extremely important'; budget and rural segments are more moderate.

questions.question: How strongly do you agree or disagree with the following statement: 'I choose organic dairy milk because it is easier on my stomach than conventional milk.'
questions.insight: Top response: Agree (32.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused and lactose-intolerant segments agree more; value seekers and budget families are neutral or disagree due to cost focus.

questions.question: Which of the following most often triggers you to buy organic dairy milk?
options: I run out and need to restock for daily use
It's on sale or I have a coupon
I'm buying it for a specific recipe or meal
A health or wellness goal prompts me to buy it
My children or family ask for it
I see it in the store and decide to pick it up

data.label: I run out and need to restock for daily use
It's on sale or I have a coupon
I'm buying it for a specific recipe or meal
A health or wellness goal prompts me to buy it
My children or family ask for it
I see it in the store and decide to pick it up

questions.insight: Top response: I run out and need to restock for daily use (32.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Daily-use restocking dominates across all personas, especially Budget Family and Rural Practical. Health-focused and Eco-conscious boost wellness-triggered purchases. Value Seekers and Budget Family lift sale/coupon trigger.

questions.question: Before buying organic dairy milk, where do you typically look for information or compare options? Select all that apply.
options: I don't usually look for information before buying

data.label: I don't usually look for information before buying

questions.insight: Top response: In-store labels and packaging (62.00%).
questions.distributionNote: In-store labels are universal; online and social channels driven by Young Professionals, Tech Enthusiasts, Urban Convenience. Friends/family recommendations strong across mainstream and laggard personas. Health websites boosted by Health-Focused and Eco-conscious.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, where did you buy organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Farmers' market or direct from farm

data.label: Farmers' market or direct from farm

questions.insight: Top response: Large supermarket or hypermarket (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Supermarkets dominate across all personas. Discount stores favored by Value Seekers and Budget Family. Online channels driven by Young Professionals, Tech Enthusiasts, Urban Convenience. Specialty stores and farmers' markets boosted by Health-Focused and Eco-conscious.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how many separate shopping trips did you make where you bought organic dairy milk?
options: I did not buy organic dairy milk in the last 30 days

data.label: I did not buy organic dairy milk in the last 30 days

questions.insight: Top response: 2 trips (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Most households buy 2-3 times per month. Frequent buyers include larger families and health-focused. Non-buyers include some Rural Practical and Budget Family due to price/availability.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes your household's typical restock cycle for organic dairy milk?
options: We buy only when we run out
We buy on a set schedule (e.g., same day each week)
We buy whenever we are already at the store
We buy when there is a promotion or discount
We buy in bulk to last longer

data.label: We buy only when we run out
We buy on a set schedule (e.g., same day each week)
We buy whenever we are already at the store
We buy when there is a promotion or discount
We buy in bulk to last longer

questions.insight: Top response: We buy only when we run out (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Run-out and in-store impulse purchases are common across all personas. Set schedules more common among families and health-focused. Promotion-driven buying boosted by Value Seekers and Budget Family.

questions.question: When you are standing in the store or browsing online, which ONE factor most often makes you decide to put a particular organic dairy milk into your cart?
options: It is the freshest option available
It is on sale or has a price discount
It has a longer shelf life
It is from a local or regional farm
It is a store's own brand (private label)

data.label: It is the freshest option available
It is on sale or has a price discount
It has a longer shelf life
It is from a local or regional farm
It is a store's own brand (private label)

questions.insight: Top response: It is certified organic (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Certified organic is the top driver across all personas. Freshness and local farm appeal to Health-Focused and Eco-conscious. Sale/price discount is strong among Value Seekers and Budget Family.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, approximately how much did your household spend in total on organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: $10 to under $20 (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle-income personas cluster in $10-$30 range. Luxury and Health-Focused push higher spend. Budget-conscious and Rural Practical keep spend lower.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes your typical purchase routine for organic dairy milk?
options: I buy the same organic dairy milk every time without thinking about it
I usually buy the same one, but I occasionally check for better options
I compare a few options each time before deciding
I switch brands or products often based on price or availability

data.label: I buy the same organic dairy milk every time without thinking about it
I usually buy the same one, but I occasionally check for better options
I compare a few options each time before deciding
I switch brands or products often based on price or availability

questions.insight: Top response: I usually buy the same one, but I occasionally check for better options (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Habitual buying is strong among Brand Loyalists and Retired. Occasional checking is common across all. Price-driven switching is higher among Value Seekers and Budget Family.

questions.question: Which of the following would you consider a non-negotiable requirement when buying organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

data.label: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

questions.insight: Top response: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones) (82.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-Focused, Eco-Conscious, and Luxury Buyers drive high certification and pasture-raised; Budget Family and Value Seekers still prioritize no additives and consistency.

questions.question: When choosing organic dairy milk, which single sensory or label cue most strongly signals to you that the milk is fresh and high quality?
options: A 'best before' date far in the future

data.label: A 'best before' date far in the future

questions.insight: Top response: A rich, creamy taste (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Taste-driven personas (Health-Focused, Luxury, Young Professional) favor creamy taste; certification seal resonates with Eco-Conscious and Brand Loyalists; shelf-life cue important for Rural Practical and Budget Family.

questions.question: Which of the following claims or certifications would most increase your trust in an organic dairy milk product? Select all that apply.
options: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification

data.label: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification

questions.insight: Top response: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification (72.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Eco-Conscious and Health-Focused drive sustainability and welfare claims; mainstream personas trust official organic seals; local origin appeals to Rural Practical and Brand Loyalists.

questions.question: Which of the following packaging formats would you most prefer for the organic dairy milk you buy for your household?
options: Chilled, refrigerated bottle (e.g., plastic or glass)

Shelf-stable carton (does not need refrigeration until opened)

questions.insight: Top response: Chilled, refrigerated carton (e.g., half-gallon / 2-liter) (42.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Urban Convenience and Young Professionals prefer chilled cartons; Budget Families lean family-size; Rural Practical and Tech Enthusiasts show some interest in shelf-stable; single-serve favored by on-the-go personas.

questions.question: If you could not find an organic dairy milk that meets all your preferences, which trade-off would you be most willing to make?

storyline_notes: Adapted for a perishable consumable: replaced any replacement/upgrade beat with a restock cycle beat in buying_behavior.
Added a purchase_cycle beat to capture the frequent restocking nature of milk, which is essential for this category.
In consumer_profile, kept the canonical five beats but emphasized lactose intolerance and digestive comfort in need_state, reflecting the regional driver.
In buying_behavior, placed spend after decision_drivers and before repurchase to keep money late but before the more reflective routine question.
In preferences_expectations, placed format_packaging after quality_cues and claims_credentials because pack size is a concrete preference that follows quality and certification considerations.
In satisfaction_future_intent, kept the canonical six beats, with switching before advocacy to keep the more sensitive switching question earlier than the advocacy question, which is more positive.
